note: Shared redaction vectors. CLAUDE.md: a rule implemented in both JavaScript and Python gets ONE fixture that both implementations run. Before this file existed they were pinned by two DISJOINT hand-written lists, every vector in each carrying exactly one '@' -- so D-SINK-1 (a password tail surviving into the host position when the password contains an un-encoded '@') was invisible to both. The two renderings differ on purpose: the helper emits scheme://host, Model emits the bare host. So a vector pins the PROPERTY, not the formatting: the host must appear, and no fragment listed in mustNotAppear may. R32a' (2026-10-22, D-SINK-29): the FREE-TEXT rule prints the RFC host -- the authority ends at the first '/', '?', '#' or whitespace, its userinfo at the LAST '@' within it, and the printed host is cut at the first ':', ';', '=' or '&' -- and WITHHOLDS it, as the one token `[host withheld]`, when that host has no dot and an '@' follows the authority. A DISPLAY sink (sourceLabel, hostOf) prints the RFC host unconditionally. Where the two differ a vector carries `rfcHost` (and `displayMustNotAppear`) for the display check; `host` is always what the free-text redactors print, and an empty `host` requires no host at all. R32a'' (2026-10-22, D-SINK-32, D-SINK-33): the run and the authority end at ONE enumerated whitespace class (tests/fixtures/url-whitespace.json) in both mirrors; `'`, `"`, `<` and `>` never end a run and are trailing punctuation (`.,;:!?)]'"<>`), which both mirrors strip off the run's end and put back after the host, so the model restores a sentence's final `.` as the helper always did; and the predicate's second arm withholds a NON-NUMERIC port followed by a later `@`. A vector may carry `js` and `py`, the EXACT output of Model.redactUrls and of the helper's redact_urls, where the formatting is the point (the restored punctuation) or the output is an accepted cost that must be seen rather than described: `accepted` names the board id. D-SINK-34 is that cost -- a whitespace character INSIDE a password ends the run, so the username and the password's tail print, in both mirrors, one vector per class member the ruling names; D-SINK-35 is the other -- a dotted username before a digits-only password prefix reads as host and port.
credentialsAreFake: Every credential here is invented and every host is under the reserved .test TLD. Never put a real provider value in this file.

R32a': '&' ends the printed host too (RFC reg-name admits it), so a parameter glued to the host never prints -- free text on purpose, as the ';' and '=' vectors
